references.text: These verses continue the story of Terah and his family, including Abram, and their journey from Ur of the Chaldeans to Haran.
Here begins the account of God's call to Abram and his obedient departure from Haran, which is a direct continuation of Terah's family history.
God changes Abram's name to Abraham ('father of many nations'), marking an important development in the covenant history for Terah's son.
Joshua reminds the people that Terah, the father of Abraham and Nahor, lived on the other side of the Euphrates and served other gods.
The genealogy in Chronicles mentions Abram (Abraham) as a descendant of Terah, confirming the family line.
Isaiah encourages the people to look to Abraham as their ancestor and Sarah who gave birth to them, with reference to Abraham's origins.
By faith, Abraham was obedient when called to go out to a place he would later receive as an inheritance, linking back to Abram's background and family.
A theological parallel in God's guidance of salvation history through genealogies and age references at the transition between eras.
